newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen ruling party secures election victory.
newsitem.headline: Yemen ruling party secures election victory.

text.p: Yemen's ruling General People's Congress (GPC) said on Monday it won 187 seats in the 301-member parliament at the end of vote-counting in the first elections since a 1994 civil war nearly tore the country apart.

GPC secretary-general Abdul-Karim al-Iryani also told reporters 39 independents had joined the GPC making it the single largest bloc in parliament. Many of them are GPC party officials who stood as independents in the April 27 elections.

Iryani, also deputy prime minister and minister of foreign affairs, said the Islah Party, the GPC's Islamist junior coalition partner, had won 54 seats. He said that six independents had decided to join it under an alliance.
He said five seats went to two opposition parties and the rest to independents.
The Supreme Elections Committee (SEC) is expected to announce final results of the election later on Monday.
Islah has accused the SEC of bias, threatening court action in an election marred by shooting incidents that killed 22 people.

In united Yemen's first elections in 1993, the GPC won 123, Islah 62, and the main opposition Yemen Socialist Party (YSP) 56. Independents won 47 seats while the rest went to Baathist and Nasserite parties.
The YSP, some of whose leaders launched the secessionist bid that triggered the 1994 civil war, and the three others boycotted this year's polls to protest alleged irregularities.
The government has denied opposition claims that military and security personnel were used to fix the poll registration process before the arrival of international election monitors.
